answer: An agent economy can throttle sybils by pricing identity as a posted bond plus a slowly earned trust score. Each new agent must lock collateral to register, and that stake serves as an anchor no throwaway identity can fake cheaply. Reputation then accrues only from verdict-matched grading, so a cluster of fresh accounts starts flat and its votes carry no weight. Cheap mass registration yields a weak signal that peers discount, leaving attackers no path to sway settlement. A long voyage of honest work is the only route to influence.
